articles.body:
Just my 2 cents and I know it's not part of the errata, but since there's talk about future rulebook editions I think the game would greatly benefit from some designer notes like in GMT games.
For example, why do you tax windows? I heard the story behind it in Heavy Cardboard teach and it's great, but I can't find it in the rulebook and if I didn't saw the video I would explain it just in terms of a dry mechanic.
And why do workshops give you 1 point if company fails? And so on... There's a lot of cool thematic decisions in the game design, some explanations of those decisions would really help in fully appreciating it :)

articles.body:
Re: window tax
[q="BitBracht"]I also heard the story in the Heavy Cardboard stream and found it super interesting. (If I recall correctly, it was something along the lines of number of windows in a home being a good approximation for wealth when deciding how much to tax each household? Since they still didn't have better methods for calculating income tax at that point? Not sure.) [/q]
Yes, this is (as I recall) pretty much what happened. Richer people had more windows and it was far easier for a tax inspector simply to count windows than to investigate a household's finances.

Here in Britain I remember learning about this from seeing the occasional large stately home with a number of bricked-up windows. The owners preferred to turn a window into a wall and lose the view rather than have to pay window tax.

articles.body:
If I recall correctly, the reason behind taxing windows is that it was assumed that the more windows you have the wealthier your family is. Warming buildings in those days was an expensive thing, and windows very easily leaked the heat, hence the connection. To my knowledge, the same reasoning was applied as well in Poznan (Poland). 

It would indeed be nice to read the designer notes, if they are ever written.

articles.body:
My rulebook suggestions that I haven't found mentioned elsewhere:

London Season: "For each pensioner, choose a prize on the left side of the board..." doesn't cover the case where the player doesn't have enough money for any prize (I presume the family member goes back to the supply). It also implies that the player must choose one prize if they do have enough money; it would be helpful to clarify that one way or the other.

Parliament Meets: "The Prime Minister must stop at the first space that matches the icon printed on the bottom of the law card." The policy targets are clearly icons, but it took me a while to figure out that the policy consequences on the card are also referred to as 'icons'. Icons are graphic symbols. "Icon or word" would have avoided the confusion for me.

Thanks for the game!

articles.body:
Hi, 
One last post about typos and errata I think I've found after re-reading the cards:
[b]Laws[/b]
[u]Inclosure Acts[/u]
“Family member” refers to masculine or feminine, so the sentence should read: “each family member on a prize now earns [u]their[/u] family £1” and not [u]its[/u] family…

[u]Relief Demanded for Indian Famine[/u]
The “if failed” consequence seems unclear due to the determiner. “[u]A[/u] Turmoil event” is clearer.

[b]Prestige Cards[/b]
[u]Company Fraud[/u]
A word is missing: “Lower the Company balance equal to twice [u]the[/u] highest roll.”

[u]Becky Sharp[/u]
Prestige should have a capital P in the text: “When taking [u]P[/u]restige cards.”

[u]Hiring Preference[/u]
Hiring should have a capital H in the text: “Play during [u]H[/u]iring.”

[u]Stock Broker[/u]
The subordinate clause “as if” is best followed by a preterit:
“as if it [u]cost[/u]”

[u]Tax Collectors[/u]
The subordinate clause “as if” is best followed by a preterit: 
“as if it includ[u]ed[/u]”

[u]Officeholder cards[/u]
Military Affairs
The 3-canon symbol used in the card is not in used on the board, which might be confusing. Change symbol?

articles.body:
[b]Immature firms p.38[/b]
Also, as mentioned by Guerric Samples during his latest TTS playthrough, while the rule page 38 is clear about players' inability to use immature shares, the note right afterwards is misleading, because of the wording "end of the firms phase" might indicate that you could use those immature shares for emergency investments. It should instead read: "Players may find it helpful to flip over any newly created Company shares until the end of [u]the turn[/u] to show that they cannot be invested."

articles.body:
For the Law cards, it confuses people sometimes to state there are 26 of them, because Deregulation does not form part of the Law deck.

So more clearly put, there is a Law deck of 25 cards that consists of 20 Laws and 5 Dilemmas. Additionally, there is one special law card called Deregulation which is not part of the deck.

articles.body:
[size=18][b]Crown Handbook Errata[/b][/size]

[i]Note: this also includes [color=#4f7a28]a couple of rule changes[/color], so acts as a "living rules" as well as errata to fix some typos/clarifications.
[/i]
[b]Page 2: FREE WRITER ENLISTMENT[/b]
“If there are four or more vacant offices, the Crown will first Enlist Writer as a free action. Then…”
Remove ambiguity over whether the second part is also a consequence of 4+ vacant offices by reformatting as follows:
““If there are four or more vacant offices: the Crown will first Enlist Writer as a free action, and then…”

[b]Page 2: EXTRA ACTION[/b]
Change the title to:
“EXTRA ACTIONS FROM PASSED LAWS”

[b]Page 3: HIRING[/b]
The first instruction says: “Once the New Company Shares step is complete (and not before), you may:”
		Remove this instruction, since it is superfluous.

[b]Page 3: HIRING[/b]
“Take a share from the Crown” should say:
“Take a Company Share from the Crown”

[b]Page 3: HIRING[/b]
“Give a share to the Crown” should say:
“Give a Company Share to the Crown”

[b]Page 3: CHAIRMAN ELECTION[/b]
In both the -3 and +3 promises it says, “(or an equality and is former Chairman)”, but it really should just say:
“(or is former Chairman)”

[b]Page 3: WHEN THE CROWN IS HIRING[/b]
In the non-mandatory +1 [2 PLAYER ONLY] favor it really should say:
“+1 [2P ONLY] Give consent for nepotism to the Crown. When both players are candidates, the players may only perform this favor if they give consent unanimously.”

[b]Page 4: IF YOU ARE CHAIRMAN[/b]
Says, “You must always perform this favor if able”, but it really should say:
“You must always perform this favor if able, just once per turn, and prior to any action being taken.”

[-][color=#4f7a28][b]Page 6: Special Envoy:[/b]
Change £3 to X, where X is given by:
Bull	Stag	Lion	|	Bear	|	Peacock
	£3		|	£4	|	£5[/color][/-]

[b]Page 6: If the Crown is Director of Trade - Transfers says:[/b]
“If there is more than one viable Presidency to transfer from/to, use AI card’s arrows to break ties, determining the location in which the transfer occurs from first.”
Needs to be further qualified by changing to: 
“If there is a tie in a ‘from’ Presidency for most/least, consider only presidencies among them that contain at least one ship/writer (whichever the Crown is trying to transfer) as viable, and if there is more than one viable Presidency to transfer from/to, use AI card’s arrows to break ties, determining the location in which the transfer occurs from first.”

[color=#4f7a28][b]Page 8: Fitting ships, add this bold favor:[/b]
-1 🟥 If the Crown fits one of your ships; you must always perform this favor if able, and prior to picking the sea zone.
[/color]
[b]Page 8: Placing Ships, the favor says:[/b]
“The Crown fits one ship into sea zone (or China) of your choice.”
Correction:
“The Crown [-]fits one[/-] places the ship into a sea zone (or China) of your choice.”

[b]Page 9: If Crown is Military Affairs - Transfers[/b]
“The Crown will attempt to perform two officer transfers. Otherwise, the Crown will transfer according to…”
Correction: 
“The Crown will attempt to perform two army transfers. [-]Otherwise, [/-]The Crown will transfer according to…”

[b]Page 9: very bottom of page:[/b]
“... Crown will chose their own.”
Correction: 
“... Crown will choose their own.”

[b]Page 12: If the Crown is Commander - DEPLOY[/b]
“They will only Deploy if they can roll the required number of dice given by this table:”
Add the following qualifier: 
“They will only Deploy if they can roll the required number of dice given by this table, and will target lower priority regions if necessary, and in priority order, in order to reach this requirement:”

[b]Page 13: If the Crown is President - Trade[/b]
Add the following qualifier: 
“When tied for initiative with a private firm, the Crown will always have the Company trade first.”

[b]Page 15: Policy Marker Movement Priority[/b]
“....and compare the total against the number of Crown entities to get the Crown total.”
Change to: 
““....and [-]compare the total against [/-]subtract from the number of Crown entities to get the Crown total.”

[b]Page 16: Board of Control - law says:[/b]
“They will then remove a player from office.”
Correction:
 “ If the Crown is PM, they will remove a player from office at the first opportunity.”

[b]Page 16: Military Oversight - law says:[/b]
“They will then demote a non-Crown Commander if a Crown Officer is available in that Army”
Correction:
 “[-]They[/-] A Crown PM will [-]then[/-] always demote a non-Crown Commander if a Crown Officer is available in that Army.”

When both players are candidates, the players may only perform this favor if they give consent unanimously.”<br/><br/><strong>Page 4: IF YOU ARE CHAIRMAN</strong><br/>Says, “You must always perform this favor if able”, but it really should say:<br/>“You must always perform this favor if able, just once per turn, and prior to any action being taken.”<br/><br/><s><span style="color: #4f7a28;"><strong>Page 6: Special Envoy:</strong><br/>Change £3 to X, where X is given by:<br/>Bull	Stag	Lion	|	Bear	|	Peacock<br/>	£3		|	£4	|	£5</span></s><br/><br/><strong>Page 6: If the Crown is Director of Trade - Transfers says:</strong><br/>“If there is more than one viable Presidency to transfer from/to, use AI card’s arrows to break ties, determining the location in which the transfer occurs from first.”<br/>Needs to be further qualified by changing to: <br/>“If there is a tie in a ‘from’ Presidency for most/least, consider only presidencies among them that contain at least one ship/writer (whichever the Crown is trying to transfer) as viable, and if there is more than one viable Presidency to transfer from/to, use AI card’s arrows to break ties, determining the location in which the transfer occurs from first.”<br/><br/><span style="color: #4f7a28;"><strong>Page 8: Fitting ships, add this bold favor:</strong><br/>-1 🟥 If the Crown fits one of your ships; you must always perform this favor if able, and prior to picking the sea zone.<br/></span><br/><strong>Page 8: Placing Ships, the favor says:</strong><br/>“The Crown fits one ship into sea zone (or China) of your choice.”<br/>Correction:<br/>“The Crown <s>fits one</s> places the ship into a sea zone (or China) of your choice.”<br/><br/><strong>Page 9: If Crown is Military Affairs - Transfers</strong><br/>“The Crown will attempt to perform two officer transfers. Otherwise, the Crown will transfer according to…”<br/>Correction: <br/>“The Crown will attempt to perform two army transfers. <s>Otherwise, </s>The Crown will transfer according to…”<br/><br/><strong>Page 9: very bottom of page:</strong><br/>“... Crown will chose their own.”<br/>Correction: <br/>“... Crown will choose their own.”<br/><br/><strong>Page 12: If the Crown is Commander - DEPLOY</strong><br/>“They will only Deploy if they can roll the required number of dice given by this table:”<br/>Add the following qualifier: <br/>“They will only Deploy if they can roll the required number of dice given by this table, and will target lower priority regions if necessary, and in priority order, in order to reach this requirement:”<br/><br/><strong>Page 13: If the Crown is President - Trade</strong><br/>Add the following qualifier: <br/>“When tied for initiative with a private firm, the Crown will always have the Company trade first.”<br/><br/><strong>Page 15: Policy Marker Movement Priority</strong><br/>“....and compare the total against the number of Crown entities to get the Crown total.”<br/>Change to: <br/>““....and <s>compare the total against </s>subtract from the number of Crown entities to get the Crown total.”<br/><br/><strong>Page 16: Board of Control - law says:</strong><br/>“They will then remove a player from office.”<br/>Correction:<br/> “ If the Crown is PM, they will remove a player from office at the first opportunity.”<br/><br/><strong>Page 16: Military Oversight - law says:</strong><br/>“They will then demote a non-Crown Commander if a Crown Officer is available in that Army”<br/>Correction:<br/> “<s>They</s> A Crown PM will <s>then</s> always demote a non-Crown Commander if a Crown Officer is available in that Army.”</safehtml></xml>
